rule.vbs100.title: Script file could not be checked
rule.vbs100.rationale: The file is a script type that runs VBScript (.vbs, .vbe) or can contain it (.wsf, .wsc, .hta), but it could not be read. Check it manually.
rule.vbs101.title: VBScript file (.vbs)
rule.vbs101.rationale: Windows runs .vbs files with the VBScript engine. Microsoft has deprecated VBScript: it is now a Windows feature on demand that is expected to be disabled by default in a later phase and removed after that. Without VBScript, the file no longer runs.
rule.vbs102.title: Encoded VBScript file (.vbe)
rule.vbs102.rationale: .vbe files contain VBScript that was scrambled with the Script Encoder; Windows runs them with the VBScript engine ("VBScript.Encode"). The encoding does not change the language: without VBScript, the file no longer runs. The affected lines are shown after decoding the file.
rule.vbs103.title: Windows Script File (.wsf) with VBScript
rule.vbs103.rationale: The file contains a script element in VBScript (or VBScript.Encode). Windows Script Host runs it with the VBScript engine, so this part stops working once VBScript is disabled.
rule.vbs104.title: Windows Script Component (.wsc) with VBScript
rule.vbs104.rationale: The script component contains VBScript code. Programs that use the component call the VBScript engine; without VBScript, the component can no longer be used.
rule.vbs105.title: HTML application (.hta) with VBScript
rule.vbs105.rationale: The HTML application contains VBScript (script blocks, event handlers or vbscript: links). mshta.exe runs this code with the VBScript engine; without VBScript, these parts of the application stop working.
rule.vbs200.title: Script or shortcut could not be checked
rule.vbs200.rationale: The file may start VBScript but could not be read or analysed. Check it manually.
rule.vbs201.title: Script starts VBScript
rule.vbs201.rationale: The script runs a VBScript file or VBScript code – through wscript.exe or cscript.exe, by starting a .vbs/.vbe file directly or through a vbscript: command (e.g. with mshta.exe). This call fails once VBScript is disabled.
rule.vbs202.title: Script starts a script whose language is not known
rule.vbs202.rationale: The script starts a Windows Script File (.wsf), an HTML application (.hta) or a script through the Windows Script Host whose language only shows in the started file. Check whether that file uses VBScript.
rule.vbs211.title: Shortcut starts VBScript
rule.vbs211.rationale: The shortcut runs a VBScript file or VBScript code (through wscript.exe, cscript.exe or mshta.exe, or by opening a .vbs/.vbe file). Once VBScript is disabled, the shortcut no longer works.
rule.vbs212.title: Shortcut starts a script whose language is not known
rule.vbs212.rationale: The shortcut starts a .wsf or .hta file or a script through the Windows Script Host whose language only shows in the started file. Check whether that file uses VBScript.
rule.vbs300.title: Task, autostart entry, service or logon script could not be checked
rule.vbs300.rationale: The entry may start VBScript but could not be read or analysed. Check it manually.
rule.vbs301.title: Scheduled task runs VBScript
rule.vbs301.rationale: The task runs a VBScript file or VBScript code automatically. Once VBScript is disabled, the task fails – often unnoticed, because nobody watches its result.
rule.vbs302.title: Scheduled task starts a script whose language is not known
rule.vbs302.rationale: The task starts a .wsf or .hta file or a script through the Windows Script Host whose language only shows in the started file. Check whether that file uses VBScript.
rule.vbs311.title: Autostart entry runs VBScript
rule.vbs311.rationale: The entry (Run/RunOnce key, startup folder, Winlogon or Active Setup) runs VBScript automatically at startup or logon. Once VBScript is disabled, it fails at every logon.
rule.vbs312.title: Autostart entry starts a script whose language is not known
rule.vbs312.rationale: The autostart entry starts a .wsf or .hta file or a script through the Windows Script Host whose language only shows in the started file. Check whether that file uses VBScript.
rule.vbs321.title: Windows service runs VBScript
rule.vbs321.rationale: The service (or its failure command, or a service wrapper such as srvany or NSSM) runs VBScript. Once VBScript is disabled, the service no longer starts or its function fails.
rule.vbs322.title: Windows service starts a script whose language is not known
rule.vbs322.rationale: The service starts a .wsf or .hta file or a script through the Windows Script Host whose language only shows in the started file. Check whether that file uses VBScript.
rule.vbs331.title: WMI event subscription runs VBScript
rule.vbs331.rationale: A permanent WMI event consumer runs VBScript when its event occurs (ActiveScriptEventConsumer with the VBScript engine, or a command-line consumer that starts VBScript). Such subscriptions run invisibly; once VBScript is disabled, they fail. An unknown subscription can also be a sign of compromise.
rule.vbs332.title: WMI event subscription starts a script whose language is not known
rule.vbs332.rationale: A permanent WMI event consumer starts a script whose language only shows in the started file. Check the subscription and the script.
rule.vbs341.title: Logon, logoff, startup or shutdown script runs VBScript
rule.vbs341.rationale: Group Policy or the user's environment runs the script at logon, logoff, startup or shutdown, and it needs VBScript. Once VBScript is disabled, the drive mappings, printer connections or other settings it makes are missing – on every affected computer.
rule.vbs342.title: Logon, logoff, startup or shutdown script whose language is not known
rule.vbs342.rationale: The policy starts a .wsf or .hta file or a script through the Windows Script Host whose language only shows in the started file. Check whether that file uses VBScript.
rule.vbs400.title: Installer package could not be checked
rule.vbs400.rationale: The MSI package could not be read or analysed, so its custom actions are unknown. Check it manually (e.g. with Orca) for VBScript custom actions.
rule.vbs401.title: Installer package runs VBScript (custom action)
rule.vbs401.rationale: The package contains a VBScript custom action (type 6, 22, 38 or 54) that runs during installation, repair, update or removal. Once VBScript is disabled, these operations fail – typically only when they are needed, e.g. at an uninstall or repair.
rule.vbs402.title: Installer package contains a VBScript custom action (impact uncertain)
rule.vbs402.rationale: The package contains a VBScript custom action whose errors are ignored or that is not scheduled in any sequence. The operation does not stop, but whatever the script does is missing. Check what the custom action is for.
rule.vbs500.title: Event log could not be checked
rule.vbs500.rationale: The event log could not be read, so recorded VBScript use is unknown.
rule.vbs501.title: Windows recorded VBScript use
rule.vbs501.rationale: Windows logged a VBScript deprecation alert (event 4096, source VBScriptDeprecationAlert) because this program used VBScript. It is proof of actual use; the process tree shows how it was started.
rule.vbs502.title: Sysmon recorded a VBScript start
rule.vbs502.rationale: Sysmon logged the start of a process that runs VBScript (wscript.exe, cscript.exe or mshta.exe with a VBScript file or vbscript: code). It is proof of actual use; find out what started it.
rule.vbs503.title: Sysmon recorded a program loading the VBScript engine
rule.vbs503.rationale: Sysmon logged that this program loaded vbscript.dll. The program most likely runs VBScript code (e.g. embedded scripts or regular expressions); check what it uses it for.
rule.vbs901.title: Hard-coded credentials
rule.vbs901.rationale: A password, a connection-string password or credentials in a URL are written into the script or its call. Anyone who can read the file can use them. The value was masked and not stored. Move the secret into a protected store when the script is migrated.
collector.banner: {product} Collector {version} – read-only scan for VBScript dependencies
collector.help:
Usage: {program} [options]

Scans this computer for VBScript dependencies and writes one result file.
Nothing on the computer is changed and no network connection is made.

Options:
  --out <file or folder>  Where to write the result file. Default: the current
                          folder, named <computer>_<date-time>.{extension}.
                          Existing files are never overwritten.
  --path <folder>         Scan only this local folder instead of all local
                          drives (repeatable).
  --include-unc <\\server\share\folder>
                          Also scan this network path, with the rights of the
                          running account (repeatable). Network paths are never
                          scanned otherwise.
  --files-only            Scan files only; skip the registry, scheduled tasks,
                          services, WMI and event logs.
  --lang <language>       Language of the console output (default: en):
                          {languages}.
  --quiet                 Print errors only.
  --help                  Show this help.
  --version               Show the version.

Run as administrator (or as SYSTEM through GPO, Intune or an RMM tool) for a
complete scan. Exit codes: 0 = result written, 1 = error, 2 = invalid options.
collector.limited: Not running as administrator: the scan is limited because protected locations cannot be read. The result file records this.
collector.done: Done in {seconds} s: {entries} entries examined, {findings} findings.
collector.error.outputExists: {path} already exists. {product} never overwrites files – choose another output path.
collector.error.outputDirMissing: The output folder {path} does not exist.
collector.error.systemFolder: The current folder {path} is a Windows system folder. Choose where to write the result with --out – for example a network share that collects all results.
collector.error.write: The result file {path} could not be written: {message}
collector.error.pathMissing: {path} does not exist or is not a folder.
collector.error.networkPath: {path} is a network path. Network locations are only scanned when given with --include-unc.
